chapters: Focus on Early Career Talent and Recruitment

evidence.activity: Equal-opportunity and anti-discrimination policy statement covering all employees
evidence.quote: We strive to maintain a culture of diversity and inclusion in which people from all backgrounds can fully contribute to the growth and success of our business.

cross_cultural.criterion: level 1: general statement and equal-opportunity boilerplate, with no specific program behind it

evidence.activity: Disclosure of workforce gender and racial makeup
evidence.quote: In addition, of our U.S. based employees, approximately 17% are non-white, including 14% of management.
evidence.indicators: 66% of employees globally are women; 65% of management; 52% of director level and above; 17% of U.S. employees non-white; 14% of management

evidence.activity: Regional employee social committees, funded by a global social budget, hold cultural events such as Lunar New Year celebrations and a Cultural Discovery Potluck
evidence.quote: Whether at Oktoberfest in sister cities Munich and Cincinnati, FantaEurovision in Milan, Lunar New Year in Asia-Pacific offices, or a Cultural Discovery Potluck in Leuven, regional social committees create social events for everyone.

cross_cultural.criterion: borderline level 2: specific cultural social events for employees, but described as general office socializing with no figures and no inclusion purpose

cross_cultural.reason: Level 1. The 10-K offers only equal-opportunity boilerplate (E1) and workforce demographics (E2), and demographics count as a disclosure, not an activity. The report adds more demographics (new-hire race self-identification, gender pay gap) and office cultural social events run by regional committees (E3). These events are presented as general employee socializing ('to meet, socialize, build relationships, and de-stress'). They have no participation figures and no stated aim of removing barriers or including underrepresented groups. They are weaker than the level-2 example of employee networks. I was torn between 1 and 2, and the rubric says to pick the lower level. No employee resource groups, accessibility programs, multilingual or underserved-customer access, or community-bridging programs are described.

ai.notes: Rescored from scratch using the 10-K plus the 2025-2026 Corporate Responsibility Report chapters provided. Coverage is now sufficient because the report adds people sections. Report-only demographic figures (new hires ~21% non-white, ~14% of management-level new hires non-white; 6.3% uncontrolled median US gender pay gap) are disclosures, not activities. They are not listed separately to avoid double counting with E2. The report's University of Cincinnati / NIL partnerships, internships and Keeping Pace blog are early-career recruitment, not cross-cultural inclusion, so they were not counted here. The E3 quote spans line breaks in the report PDF (the original has extra spaces after 'sister cities'), so whitespace normalization may be needed for verification. Patient recruitment 'barriers' in the 10-K refers to clinical trial enrollment, not cultural or demographic access, so it was not counted.
